about: Trigger eval queries for this skill's description. A query is labelled with whether the skill should activate for it; the negatives are near-misses that share vocabulary with the skill but need something else. Split fixed so successive description edits are compared on the same ground: tune against train, judge against validation. Two labels were corrected by hand (issues #25, #24): `too long -- just the result and the options` (train) and `put the options in a table with a recommendation` (validation) are negatives here, not positives. Both committed cases were already written as standing instructions -- a dozen answers to come, `from here on` over six decisions -- and still fired 0x and 1x in three runs, with compactor silent on every run of both. Briefing holds no state: `allowed-tools` is `Read` alone, there is no config file and no session hook, so a request to answer more briefly is compliable in the current turn whether it is meant for one answer or for all of them, and nothing firing is correct. What does need this skill is the one thing the assistant cannot supply unaided -- what this project's output style actually says -- so both compensating positives ask for it to be loaded or read back, mirroring lingua's `what response language is set for this project`. Each replaced the negative that had asserted the same line the relabelled query now draws with runs behind it: `summarise the previous answer` and `condense this table`. The description still claims `when the user asks for shorter output`; that is a description-level mismatch and out of scope here -- #9 reverted a briefing rewrite and #25 does not re-authorise one.
how_to_run: `make eval` is the committed runner, but it covers only the queries a 3-sample blind-router baseline actually missed, not this whole file -- see CLAUDE.md for why 13 and not 380. To judge the rest: `skillgrade` runs a labelled set like this one and exits non-zero when the pass rate falls below a threshold. Needing nothing installed: run each query with `claude -p --output-format json` and count the runs whose transcript contains a Skill tool_use naming this skill. Cheapest of all, and closest to the router's real conditions: give a model only the name and description of every installed skill, with no bodies and no repo access, and have it pick one skill or none per query. `claude plugin eval`, which `make eval` drives, is generally available rather than early access; what it needs instead is a credential, a network and real money -- $0.142 a run, measured -- which is why it sits outside `make test` and CI does not run it. It will not reproduce this file query-for-query either: a bare query does not fire a skill, so a case is one of these queries rewritten as a realistic turn. This file stays the cheap, free, offline record.
